findings.title: Non-text content-block mapping has no test and the fake server cannot produce it
findings.description: The slice design's Result mapping rules (slice design line 137) require that "Non-text blocks are noted by type in the content, not dropped silently" — part of the same slice-909 silent-no-op family as the empty-result rule. Task 4.2 implements this, but Task 3.1's fake server enumerates only four tools (`echo`, `fail`, `sleep`, `empty`), all of which emit text or zero blocks, so Task 5's bridge tests can never exercise a non-text block. Success criterion 2 ("maps results per the Result mapping rules") therefore leaves this rule unverified. Fix is small: add one fixture tool returning a non-text block (e.g. an `ImageContent` or mixed-content tool) and one assertion in `tests/tools/test_mcp_bridge.py` that the type is named in `ToolResult.content`.

findings.title: Success criterion 6's non-SDK model dispatch demo (walkthrough §4) is deferred by design
findings.description: SC6 requires both a live `cf_workflow_status` smoke (covered by Task 8.2 and Task 9.1 step 2) and a dispatch with a tool-capable non-SDK model calling `cf_build_context` (walkthrough §4). Task 9.3 explicitly records that step 4 runs from a standard terminal (the `sq run` CLAUDECODE guard refuses inside Claude Code) and "remains open alongside 263's demo". This is a documented, justified deferral of a manual acceptance step rather than an untracked gap — recorded here so the open item is visible at review time. No task change required.
